writer: Kernel startup creates the app directory.
capture: Enumerate each app including drafts.
restore: Recreate the directory on the destination.

writer: Owner login, Clerk, invitations, owner-code commands and owner-suspend/resume write accounts and admission state.
capture: Snapshot accounts, codes and sessions.
restore: Keep accounts and admission codes. Clear owner sessions and account challenges, then reconcile suspensions.

writer: MCP and editor project creation/deletion, source saves, releases, imports, audit, OAuth and credentials share this database.
capture: Snapshot project ownership, revisions, receipts, plans, grants and audit rows.
restore: Keep catalogue and audit. Clear credentials, OAuth codes and release plans.

writer: Signup, recovery, invitations and notify enqueue mail. The worker claims, retries and records deliveries.
capture: Snapshot the live queue and history.
restore: End pending jobs and retain terminal history.

writer: Call actions enqueue requests. The worker records attempts, replies and continuation mutations. Test mode records synthetic replies.
capture: Snapshot outbox and attempts.
restore: Keep completed calls. Retire pending calls with restored-outcome-unknown and mark processing continuations interrupted.

writer: Chunked uploads, downloads, cancellation, expiry and file commit write transfer rows and receipts.
capture: Snapshot metadata and receipts.
restore: Clear unfinished transfers. Keep file receipts.

writer: Google sign-in creates a flow and the callback consumes it.
capture: Omit in-flight OAuth state.
restore: Require a new Google sign-in. The app client lives in secrets.sqlite.

writer: Standalone kernel startup and kernel app commands, including import on a Konae volume, create or reuse this private fallback key.
capture: Keep the key in restricted operator custody. Installation copies and app exports omit it.
restore: Restore ends pending mail. The next kernel start or app command can generate a new key. The konae server uses KONAE_MAIL_SECRET or KONAE_SETUP_KEY.

writer: Test mode queues local messages and reset retires them.
capture: Omit the local test queue.
restore: Start with an empty test queue.

writer: Development and test mail transports append messages.
capture: Omit transport transcripts.
restore: Start a new mailbox on first delivery.

writer: Startup, files-migrate and files-reconcile record the active store and migration state.
capture: Omit the live backend marker.
restore: Use the restored local blobs. Migrate after verification if required.

writer: A serving Kernel and offline file-store commands take the volume lock.
capture: Omit the process lock.
restore: The next process acquires its own lock.

writer: Requests, workers and commands record unfinished operations.
capture: Refuse capture until each operation finishes or is reconciled.
restore: Start with an empty journal.

writer: The copy worker records blob stamps, hashes and manifest cache.
capture: Omit the cache.
restore: Read the blobs on the next copy.

writer: Copy stages snapshots. Restore materializes a copy before installation.
capture: Omit staging.
restore: A remaining restore directory prevents startup. Repeat restore on an empty volume.

writer: The copy and restore commands record per-target diagnostics (#38).
capture: Omit local health history. Operators can place it outside the volume.
restore: Start fresh or consult the separately retained history.

writer: Restore and offline reconcile set or clear the installation hold.
capture: Omit this marker from the copy.
restore: Compute the hold from the destination revocation record.

writer: Transfers, package export/import and files-migrate stage bytes under this directory.
capture: Omit transfer payloads and scratch files.
restore: Open new transfers after restore.

writer: Folder startup and release planning rehearse schema changes on a private copy.
capture: Omit rehearsal files.
restore: Run a new plan before applying a release.

writer: Project deletion parks its folder here while removing files and catalogue entries.
capture: Omit retired projects.
restore: Leave deleted folders out of the active app list.

writer: The volume filesystem owns this directory.
capture: Exclude the filesystem recovery directory.
restore: Leave it under filesystem control.

writer: Project creation, folder installation and project deletion add or remove an app.
capture: Capture every installed folder.
restore: Keep its ID on this installation.

writer: Editor saves, releases, module_set, access tools and the folder watcher update draft and released settings.
capture: Copy settings including module options and the released snapshot.
restore: Keep draft and released revisions separate.

writer: Editor and MCP source saves, folder edits, release, import and inner restore replace source files.
capture: Copy regular source files. The writer skips dot entries except .konae. Directory names can also live in settings or legacy metadata.
restore: Keep draft sources even when dist is absent.

presence: optional for drafts, required for a published artifact
writer: Publisher, folder build and source import replace the served artifact.
capture: Copy the published tree.
restore: Keep the artifact alongside its released rules. A draft can have no dist.

writer: Publish and the local builder write the Server Artifact.
capture: Copy the manifest and bundled handlers with the release.
restore: Load the restored artifact with its matching Deployment.

writer: App writers and import create the stores below.
capture: Capture existing stores.
restore: Keep optional stores absent until used.

writer: Release, address tools, maintenance and internal backups write installation metadata.
capture: Inspect each entry under this directory.
restore: Restore the records for this installation.

writer: The app-folder generator writes support files.
capture: Keep build files in the author's folder or version control.
restore: The app-folder generator can write the shipped defaults again.

writer: The app-folder generator installs build scripts.
capture: Keep the author's build inputs separately.
restore: Restore the authored version for local builds.

writer: The app-folder generator installs the builder and SDK.
capture: Keep build tooling in the authored folder.
restore: Regenerate the default scripts from the matching version.

presence: optional until a release enables actions
writer: Server Actions, HTTP routes, schedules, call continuations, owner SQL, schema apply, import and inner restore write or replace app rows.
capture: Snapshot the live database and schema journal when present.
restore: Restore app rows, rules and schema history.

presence: optional until an app requires identity
writer: App login, Google, invitation, suspension, API-key, replay protection and enter commands update accounts, sessions and keys. Import and reconcile update access.
capture: Snapshot app accounts, links, sessions and API keys.
restore: Clear sessions and challenges, keep current keys at the cut, apply later recorded revocations.

writer: Usage flushes, Signals, retention and schedule slot/run accounting write this database. Import can replace it.
capture: Snapshot metrics, Signals, run history and schedule slots.
restore: Keep run history. The timer takes a fresh slot baseline at its first tick.

writer: Owners and kernel secret set/delete maintain signing secrets and per-app Google credentials.
capture: Snapshot installation-bound secrets.
restore: Restore to the same app. Export omits this database.

writer: File upload/delete, import and files-migrate update the index or blob store.
capture: Read the index and capture its referenced objects from the active backend.
restore: Materialize local files for the same app and owners.

writer: Internal database restore stages a replacement SQLite.
capture: Omit replacement scratch files.
restore: Use the captured live database.

writer: Upload, delete, import and files-reconcile replace metadata, owner and visibility entries.
capture: Copy the index with the bytes it names.
restore: Check index and bytes together (#38).

writer: Upload, delete, import and migration write local bytes. S3 installations use object keys instead.
capture: Fetch indexed bytes from the configured store.
restore: Install bytes locally with their original IDs.

writer: Publish, module changes and folder installation persist the Installed record.
capture: Copy the effective actions, artifact identity and deployed settings.
restore: Use the installed version with its dist.

writer: Domain, hostname and path operations claim, replace and remove address records.
capture: Copy active address records.
restore: Reload the app's addresses.

writer: MCP and kernel maintenance change the app's maintenance state.
capture: Copy the existing marker.
restore: Preserve prior app maintenance through restore and reconcile.

writer: Older editor saves wrote draft metadata here. Current saves fold it into konae.json.
capture: Copy legacy metadata when present.
restore: Read the original draft name, manifest and directory list.

writer: Data panel, import and inner restore create app recovery points.
capture: Capture records and all payloads they promise (#35).
restore: Keep each point available to restore-backup.

writer: Source save and release stage and retire source or artifact trees.
capture: Omit staged and retired generations.
restore: Use committed app and dist trees.

writer: Publish stages and swaps a migrated database.
capture: Omit release scratch and retired databases.
restore: Install the live data store.

writer: database_execute backup, import and restore-backup write the record.
capture: Copy the record with its promised payload.
restore: Keep its ID, label and holds.

writer: Data panel and backup before plain SQLite restore write a database snapshot.
capture: Copy the older flat snapshot as bytes.
restore: Use it for a database-only restore.

writer: Import and inner restore snapshot the parts they will replace.
capture: Copy recorded data and source payloads (#35).
restore: Preserve the original inner recovery point.

writer: Internal backup writes the selected data package, sources or both.
capture: Copy exact payload bytes. Each record determines its required parts.
restore: Inner restore applies the recorded scope and retains destination access as defined by import.

writer: S3FileStore, import, deletion and files-migrate write app objects.
capture: Read indexed objects from the configured backend.
restore: Restore local bytes without the original bucket.

writer: Copy worker writes manifests and bytes. Pruning removes expired points.
capture: Keep each configured repository outside the live data root.
restore: Read the selected point from that repository.

writer: Account suspension/resume, API key revocation and offline administration append records on each target.
capture: Protect the per-target ledger and its start marker independently of the cut.
restore: Reconcile latest states. An unavailable or invalid record holds the installation.

writer: The operator manages mail secrets, SMTP/Resend, copy encryption and S3 credentials. Konae also uses setup and optional Clerk configuration.
capture: Keep these in operator custody outside installation copies and app exports.
restore: Provision matching keys and configuration before restore or service startup.

writer: Signup, login and invitations write identity.sqlite and mail.
capture: Capture account state, app policy and secrets.
restore: Invalidate open sessions and links.

writer: The action executor and schedules mutate app rows. Signals, schedule runs and notify write Usage or mail.
capture: Capture database.sqlite, usage.sqlite, mail.sqlite, declarations and settings.
restore: Restore the stored program and recorded work.

writer: Publish installs page bindings. Page rendering reads action results.
capture: Capture declarations, dist and the released record.
restore: Resolve page paths using the applied release.

writer: The file API writes the index, blobs and audit.
capture: Capture index, bytes, settings and app identities.
restore: Apply file ownership and fileAccess.

writer: The publisher installs bundles. Function calls can write app rows, idempotency receipts and Usage.
capture: Capture the Server Artifact, release, app data and Usage.
restore: Load handlers from the restored artifact. Start workers on demand.

writer: Call actions enqueue requests and the worker applies replies.
capture: Capture calls.sqlite, app rows, Usage and signing secrets.
restore: Retire pending calls. Check the receiver before issuing a replacement.

writer: Release installs routes. HTTP action execution can mutate rows and API key use updates identity.
capture: Capture release, rows, app identity, Usage and secrets.
restore: Restore routes, key grants and later revocations.

writer: module_set saves SEO options. Page rendering derives tags and sitemap.
capture: Capture settings, addresses, published pages and their declared data.
restore: Generate responses from restored settings.

writer: Actions, Functions, schedules and Calls record execution counts, outcomes and latency.
capture: Capture usage.sqlite with app data.
restore: Restore recorded usage without changing app rules.

writer: SQLite creates sidecars for a database with a declared policy.
capture: Read committed rows through SQLite. Omit raw sidecars.
restore: Let SQLite create new journals as needed.

writer: Atomic record, index and blob writers create a temporary sibling before rename.
capture: Omit unfinished files beside a known destination.
restore: Use the committed destination.

writer: Package install stages one uploaded object before placing it in the active file store.
capture: Omit partial imports.
restore: Recover committed indexed bytes.

writer: The maintenance command writes a sibling before replacing the marker.
capture: Omit unfinished marker writes.
restore: Use maintenance.json.
